# Overview {.unnumbered}

_One 2-hour session_

:::{.callout-note title="Learning Goals" collapse="false"}
After this lesson, you should be able to:

* Explain the differences between time series and repeated measures
* Clean and prepare time series for further analysis
* Explain what trend and seasonality are
* Decompose a time series into trend, seasonal, and remainder components
* Use statistical models to forecast future values of a time series
* Explain what partial pooling is
* Use R to fit a hierarchical model with a partially pooled intercept
:::

This workshop is an overview of statistical methods for working with datasets
collected over time or for which time is a key component. We’ll explain two
common kinds of temporal datasets: measurements taken at many time points for
just one or a few subjects (time series) and measurements taken at just a few
time points for many subjects (longitudinal or repeated measures). For each
case, we’ll introduce models and techniques that are good starting points for
more sophisticated analyses, such as autoregressive models and hierarchical
(mixed effects) models. We’ll also discuss themes and concerns common to both
cases, such as autocorrelations, trends, and seasonality. While the examples
will focus on temporal datasets, many of the methods and models generalize to
or have extensions for serial correlation in other contexts, such as in spatial
datasets.
